findings.title: Do not change notification preferences through an unauthenticated GET action
findings.body: The new GET route immediately changes the logged-in user's notification level, using only the session cookie and a predictable topic URL. GET requests do not receive Rails' normal CSRF-token protection, and this action also skips the XHR check. An external site can therefore cause a logged-in visitor to unsubscribe from a topic by navigating them to this URL, without their consent. Serve the confirmation page on GET and perform the preference change through a CSRF-protected POST, or use an appropriately scoped signed unsubscribe token.

findings.title: Record unsubscribe as an explicit notification preference change
findings.body: Saving notification_level directly bypasses TopicUser.change, which sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed and records notifications_changed_at. For a topic-user record whose reason is still nil, TopicUser.update_last_read can subsequently overwrite the unsubscribed regular or muted level with tracking once the reading-time threshold is reached. Thus reading the topic after unsubscribing can undo the choice automatically. Apply the new level through the existing preference-change API so the explicit choice is preserved.

findings.title: Handle users without an existing topic-user record
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, but the next statement unconditionally reads its notification_level. Although sending a notification email creates a record for its recipient, the unsubscribe URL is not bound to that recipient: someone opening a forwarded email while logged into another account, or opening the URL before interacting with the topic, may have no record. The endpoint then returns a server error instead of unsubscribing. Treat a missing record as the default notification level and create it through TopicUser.change.
